headline: UK Data Centre Covenant links strategic support to energy, community, environmental and security tests
summary: HM Treasury published a Data Centre Covenant on 28 October 2026. All data centres are encouraged to meet its tests; projects designated strategic must meet them when seeking enhanced government support. The tests cover energy-system costs and flexibility, local-benefit plans, efficient energy and water use, annual reporting for strategic sites, UK jobs and supply chains, and secure compute. New facilities are expected to achieve PUE of 1.3 or better. In return, government describes faster or reallocated grid connections and a tightly controlled route to temporary on-site generation for exceptionally strategic projects when other routes cannot provide capacity in time. The government estimates the UK will need 6 GW of AI data-centre capacity by 2030. These are policy terms and a government estimate, not evidence of implementation, capacity delivered or measured outcomes.
